notes:
CIRCUIT: a simple rectangle. A top rail at y~390 runs from the left column (x~157) right to (557,390); a 2 kOhm resistor #0 sits in it between x=394 and x=488. Two voltage sources hang between the top and bottom rails in parallel: 20 mV #2 on the left column (x~157) and 5 V #3 on the second column (x~296). The right column (x~557) carries the 4 uF capacitor #1 down from the top rail to the bottom rail at (557,603), where the GND symbol #5 hangs below. The bottom rail at y~605 runs from the left column right to (557,603) with the 5 mH inductor #4 in it between x=374 and x=460.

NET MAP (4 nets, 11 terminals):
  n1 = top rail left of the resistor: 20 mV top 2.0, 5 V top 3.0, 2 kOhm left 0.0.
  n2 = top rail right of the resistor plus the upper part of the right column: 2 kOhm right 0.1, 4 uF top plate 1.0.
  n3 = bottom rail left of the inductor: 20 mV bottom 2.1, 5 V bottom 3.1, 5 mH left 4.0.
  0  = bottom rail right of the inductor plus the lower part of the right column and the ground stem: 5 mH right 4.1, 4 uF bottom plate 1.1, GND 5.0.

SITE DECISIONS - there is no wire crossing anywhere on this sheet; every intersection is a plain T or a corner, so no junction/crossing judgement call arose:
  S0 (289,393) JUNCTION - CRITICAL. The 5 V source's column drops out of the top rail; clean T, no dot needed. The alternative reading would strand 3.0 on a one-terminal net and leave the 5 V source with no path to the top rail.
  S17 (298,606) JUNCTION - CRITICAL. Same column meeting the bottom rail; clean T. The alternative would strand 3.1.
  S16 (558,603) JUNCTION - CRITICAL. The bottom rail's right end meets the right column, which continues down into the GND symbol; clean corner/T with a slightly fatter blob (dot=2.0). Reading it any other way would either leave the circuit ungrounded or strand the capacitor's bottom plate.
  S19 (415,635) - the '5mH' label brushing the inductor; left at the default junction, no terminal on it.
  Non-critical label ink left at default: S1/S2/S4/S5 (the '2KOhm' under the resistor), S7/S8 (the '4uF' beside the capacitor, whose first stroke touches the plates), S9/S10 (the '5V' beside source #3), S11/S14/S15 (the '20mV' beside source #2). None carries a terminal after the port fix below.

PORT FIX (one, the classic value-label error):
  #0 Resistor 2 kOhm: t1 was on p1@(473,413), a stroke of the handwritten '2KOhm' that brushes the bottom edge of the resistor's box - that produced the two one-terminal nets n2={0.1} and n3={1.0} in the tracer output. Repointed t1 -> p5@(488,389), the real right-hand lead, which runs on to (557,390) and down the right column to the capacitor's top plate. t0 stays on p0@(394,390). Both one-terminal-net warnings are cleared by this single fix; nothing else needed changing.

NOTE ON THE CIRCUIT ITSELF: the 20 mV source #2 and the 5 V source #3 are drawn directly in parallel (both between n1 and n3, with only plain wire between them - no series element on either rail between x=157 and x=296). Two ideal voltage sources of different value in parallel is electrically inconsistent, but it is unambiguously what the drawing shows: I checked the top rail at S0 and the bottom rail at S17 in the crops and both are clean Ts with no hop or break, and there is no un-annotated component between the two columns on either rail. ERC accepts it (it flags only a source with BOTH terminals on one net). Recorded as drawn.

CLASSES: all six symbols match their labels - Resistor 2 kOhm (#0, zig-zag), Capacitor 4 uF (#1, two parallel plates), V-DC 20 mV (#2) and V-DC 5 V (#3) (circles with +/-), Inductor 5 mH (#4, coil), GND (#5, three bars). Nothing looks mis-classified. No bridges dropped, no merges, no unconnected leads.
